# Productive Efficiencies
# Saving-Investment Rates
He wrote:
"The equilibrium level of economic activity, the level at which the general economic conditions of any nation stand, depends upon two essential factors which must always be present – the growth of population, on the one hand, and the productive efficiencies, on the other. These two factors combine to determine the general economic equilibrium. They form the basic data on which all economic policy and planning must always be based.
The third factor, saving-investment rates, does not always stand in clear isolation, for they are never more than a shadow of the growth of population and the level of productive efficiencies. For the saving-investment rate is but the shadow, or reflection, of the first two."
